newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian king would work for ethnic unification.
newsitem.headline: Albanian king would work for ethnic unification.

text.p: Albania's King Leka, back from exile to seek restoration of the monarchy, pledged on Tuesday to work to reunify ethnic Albanians from Serbia's Kosovo and throughout the southern Balkans.

"I think, in the interests of all parties in the Balkans, the reunification of the Albanian areas and the Albanian nation as such is important. It would certainly be a stabilising factor in the long run," he told Reuters in an interview.
He said he believed that such a reunification could be achieved by dialogue, adding that the last thing anyone needs is another conflict in the Balkans.

Leka, who returned from 58 years in exile this month as widespread violent unrest following the collapse of fraudulent investment funds pushed Albania to the brink of anarchy, has won the promise of a referendum on the return of the monarchy from President Sali Berisha.

He said he thought the vote would be held alongside the early general election Berisha agreed by the end of June as the condition for forming a government of national unity to stop the slide into chaos.
Leka said he believed a reunification of ethnic Albanians throughout the Balkans could be achieved by political pressure, dialogue and negotiations.

"It will take time. It's not something we can envisage overnight or even over the next few years. But I think that with the proper conditions, the proper pressures -- they may be economic pressures, they may be political pressures, they may be whatever -- with proper dialogue we can come to some kind of agreement," he said.
"The last thing we need is another conflict in the Balkans. The Balkans have a habit of being a powder-keg and certainly it would be in no one's interest to light a fuse," he added.
Leka said his role was as king of all Albanians and this would remain his stand.

Some 90 percent of the two million people living in the Serbian region of Kosovo are ethnic Albanians, as are nearly a third of Macedonia's two million population. There are also sizeable ethnic Albanian communities in Greece and the Yugoslav republic of Montenegro. Albania has a 3.4 million population.

"Is it right that a large country, an economically powerful country like Germany, should be allowed to reunite and yet our small nation should be split as it is. We didn't create this problem, this was imposed on us. Let us try and balance the moral justifications on both sides," Lek said.
Leka said if the referendum came out in favour of a return of the monarchy, he would not want a coronation but would "automatically move into harness and get down to trying to rebuild the country".
He said it would be irresponsible for the new government not to rule as a coalition and it would have to devote itself to rebuilding the infrastructure of Europe's poorest state.
The 58-year-old chain-smoker -- "I should pay royalties to Rothmans," he joked -- said he had found the reception he had received in the past two weeks around Albania emotionally draining.
And if the referendum rejected a return of the monarchy?
"Then I think I can lay down the burden. Legitimacy has been returned to the hands of the people, and I'll become an Albanian citizen."
